_comment: The content and mode settings that choose what a part shows (lib/part-look-modes.mjs), as rules over the parts a block's locators find in the draft. The framework database gives these settings no CSS property or part, so the look pairing cannot place them; each names the setting it writes and the draft evidence that decides it (a part the draft draws or does not draw, the part's own words, a computed value). A rule whose setting the database does not hold for the block is a gap row; a setting that is not listed here is never written by the route.

rules.gap: the block holds one button action for every card; where the draft's button does different things per product, the catalogue writes each product's own action (_sgs_card_cta_action, add or page) and the card reads it with cardContentSource product (includes/product-card-per-product.php), so this setting is only the action of a product with none

the block holds one primary-button style (primary, secondary or outline) for every card, and the per-product reader holds a product's button words and action, not its style; the draft styles its button per product

rules.note: the per-product badge, price note and button words the catalogue writes (_sgs_card_*) render only in this mode
the stars and count are the product's own reviews (includes/product-card-live-fill.php); a product with none shows no rating row while noReviewsText is empty, which the route never writes (D-5)

woocommerce/product-filter-chips._comment: The shop's filter chips (F-6): a count drawn inside a chip is the chips block's count pill. Which chip is the 'all' choice and whether one chip is pressed at a time are not read here (the rail rule's segmented row decides the one-choice look).

sgs/account._comment: The signed-in account views (surface my-account-in). Each switch turns on the block's own view the draft draws: its orders as a list of cards (not a table), each card's thumbnails, an order's own page, and the details form's phone field and marketing tick. The menu's per-tab counts are not decided here: which tab is the orders tab would be read from its words.
